title: Candidate advancement in the controller
statement: Let $C$ and $D$ be finite-state Boolean Turing machines with positive numbers of work tapes, and choose states $c_e,c_x$ of $C$ and $d_e,d_x$ of $D$. For any Boolean input word $w$ and candidate word $s$, the controller formed from these machines has a time $t\le 2|s|+|w|+5$ at which, starting in its advance phase with $s$ on the candidate tape and all other work tapes blank, it reaches the advance phase's return state with $s$ replaced by $s$ followed by one $1$ if $|s|\le |w|$, and by $s$ otherwise. At every time $j\le t$, the controller's state is different from its anchor state.
hypotheses_covered: $C$ and $D$ are finite-state Boolean Turing machines
replaced:
There is a time $t \le 2\abs{s} + \abs{w} + 5$ after which the controller,
from its advance seam carrying the candidate $s$, has replaced $s$ by one
split-search step applied to $s$ (appending a $1$ exactly within the input
range, and stalling otherwise) and reached the advance phase's return seam;
the trace avoids the anchor.
